title: AST/GOT Detection Assay
author: Zumira Carneiro
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.k92cz8e

steps.title: Prepare Reagent 1+3 mixture
steps.instruction: Add 0.300 mL Reagent 3 to 24 mL Reagent 1 in a bottle, mix thoroughly. The mixture is stable for 21 days at 2–8 °C and for 24 h at 15–25 °C if uncontaminated. For a smaller volume, combine Reagent 3 and Reagent 1 at a ratio of 1 part to 80 parts.

steps.title: Add mixture to test tube
steps.instruction: In a labeled test tube (“test” or “Calibrator”), add 0.160 mL of the Reagent 1+3 mixture.

steps.title: Add sample and incubate
steps.instruction: Add 0.020 mL of the sample or enzyme calibrator, homogenize, then incubate in a water bath set to 37 ± 0.2 °C for 5 minutes (the tube may be held up to 30 minutes before adding Reagent 2).

steps.title: Add Reagent 2 and transfer
steps.instruction: Add 0.400 mL Reagent 2, homogenize, and immediately transfer the mixture to a cuvette maintained at 37 ± 0.2 °C; let stand for 1 minute.

steps.title: Perform water blank
steps.instruction: Measure a water blank at 340 nm.

steps.title: Record kinetic absorbance
steps.instruction: Measure the initial absorbance (A1) at 340 nm, start the timer, and measure the absorbance again after 2 minutes (A2).

steps.title: Calculate AST activity
steps.instruction: Calculate activity using DA/min = (A1‑A2)/2. If all assay conditions are met (wavelength 340 nm, cuvette temperature 37 ± 0.2 °C, 10 mm path length, pass band ≤2 nm, stray light ≤0.1 %), apply the theoretical factor 1746. Use a calibrator (e.g., Labtest Diagnostica Calibra series) when any correlated parameter is altered.
